title: Trump: Guccifer 2.0 goes public, launches DCLeaks and sends DNC docs to online media
description_short: Trump: Guccifer 2.0 goes public, launches DCLeaks and sends DNC docs to online media
description_medium: The TrumpFile timeline says Russian military-intelligence hackers used the Guccifer 2.0 identity to send documents stolen from the Democratic National Committee to journalists. On June 15, 2016, The Smoking Gun’s editor William Bastone received an email with files marked “CONFIDENTIAL.” The timeline also describes DCLeaks distributing documents over the following weeks; attribution to the GRU should be understood as the source’s account.
description_long: In June 2016, William Bastone, editor of the investigative site The Smoking Gun, received an email from someone calling himself Guccifer 2.0 with a small cache of Democratic National Committee documents marked “CONFIDENTIAL.” The sender claimed to have hacked the DNC and said he was Romanian. The TrumpFile timeline identifies the persona as a front for Russian GRU hackers and says the account contacted journalists, while the separate DCLeaks site began releasing documents in June and July. The material was later part of a wider sequence of releases that included WikiLeaks’ July 22 publication. The timeline estimates that Guccifer 2.0, DCLeaks and WikiLeaks together released more than 150,000 emails belonging to over a dozen Democrats during 2016. The account describes how stolen political material reached media organizations during the campaign; it does not establish that every outlet knew the source or coordinated with the hackers. The GRU attribution and total volume are claims reported by the supplied timeline, whose linked entry points to further coverage of the hacking operation.

preserved_fields.title: Trump: Guccifer 2.0 goes public, launches DCLeaks and sends DNC docs to online media
preserved_fields.description_short: Trump: Guccifer 2.0 goes public, launches DCLeaks and sends DNC docs to online media

notes: The linked timeline provides the email, recipient, document releases and its GRU attribution. The description attributes the identity claim to that source rather than implying The Smoking Gun verified the sender.

title: Trump: FBI Twitter account infiltrated by Trump propaganda, sparks internal investigation
description_short: Trump: FBI Twitter account infiltrated by Trump propaganda, sparks internal investigation
description_medium: The FBI’s verified Records Vault account resumed posting on October 30, 2016, after more than a year without activity, and linked to records about Fred Trump. In the following days it posted links about Hillary Clinton and earlier investigations. The FBI opened an internal inquiry on November 3. The records were already public; the linked account does not identify who authorized the posts or report the inquiry’s findings.
description_long: Near the end of the 2016 presidential campaign, the FBI’s verified “FBI Records Vault” account began posting again after more than a year of inactivity. On October 30, it linked to an eight-page file about Fred Trump; during the next three days it posted links to longer files concerning Hillary Clinton and past investigations. The documents were already publicly available, but the timing and selection of posts prompted scrutiny. The FBI opened an internal investigation into activity on its verified Twitter accounts on November 3. The linked timeline says it was unclear what became of that inquiry and notes that the posts remained visible. It does not name the account operator, show that an outsider accessed the account, or establish that the posts were directed by Donald Trump or his campaign. The episode therefore supports an account of election-period use of an official FBI channel followed by internal review, not the headline’s claim that the account was infiltrated by Trump propaganda. The investigation’s findings and any access logs are needed to establish authorization and motive.

preserved_fields.title: Trump: FBI Twitter account infiltrated by Trump propaganda, sparks internal investigation
preserved_fields.description_short: Trump: FBI Twitter account infiltrated by Trump propaganda, sparks internal investigation

notes: The linked entry confirms the posting sequence and the FBI inquiry, but does not identify who authorized the posts, report findings, or substantiate infiltration or coordination with Trump. The headline and corruption classification remain unsupported by the available evidence.
proposed_correction: Retitle this as an FBI Records Vault posting and internal-investigation episode unless inquiry findings establish unauthorized access or Trump-campaign coordination; classify it only if the evidence supports a specific harm.

title: Donald Trump tries to kill Syrian President Bashar Assad
description_short: Donald Trump tries to kill Syrian President Bashar Assad
description_medium: After a 2017 chemical attack in Syria, Trump reportedly told Defense Secretary Jim Mattis he wanted the military to kill Syrian President Bashar al-Assad. Mattis acknowledged the request but told aides he would not order an assassination. Trump later said he had wanted to “take him out,” while Mattis opposed it. The account describes a request, not an operation carried out.
description_long: The supplied timeline places Trump’s request after the April 4, 2017 chemical attack in Syria, which U.S. intelligence attributed to the Syrian government. It says Trump told Defense Secretary Jim Mattis he wanted the military to kill President Bashar al-Assad. Mattis acknowledged the request but told aides he would not order an assassination. Bob Woodward first reported the exchange in his 2018 book Fear; Trump denied it at the time, calling the account fiction and saying an assassination had never been discussed. In a September 2020 Fox News interview, Trump said he would have preferred to “take him out,” adding that Mattis had opposed the idea. The exact date of the original conversation is not known in the supplied account. The record therefore describes a reported presidential request and later public remarks, not an assassination attempt or military operation. It also distinguishes Trump’s initial denial of Woodward’s account from his later statement that he had wanted Assad removed. The source does not describe any order being issued to military forces or any action taken against Assad.

preserved_fields.title: Donald Trump tries to kill Syrian President Bashar Assad
preserved_fields.description_short: Donald Trump tries to kill Syrian President Bashar Assad

notes: The linked timeline reports a request and Mattis’s refusal, plus Trump’s later comments. No assassination attempt or military operation is documented; the event date of the reported conversation is unknown.
proposed_correction: Retitle this as Trump’s reported request to kill Assad and Mattis’s refusal, since the available account does not document an attempt or operation.

title: Trump: White nationalist kills 23 people at a Walmart in Texas
description_short: Trump: White nationalist kills 23 people at a Walmart in Texas
description_medium: A 21-year-old white nationalist attacked a Walmart in El Paso, Texas, on August 3, 2019, killing 23 people and injuring 23 others. The supplied draft says the attacker was influenced by an earlier extremist’s manifesto and wrote a manifesto of his own. The linked timeline returned no article text, so the entry’s Trump framing and the manifesto’s details remain unverified.

preserved_fields.title: Trump: White nationalist kills 23 people at a Walmart in Texas
preserved_fields.description_short: Trump: White nationalist kills 23 people at a Walmart in Texas

notes: The linked timeline returned HTTP 202 without article text. The packet does not name the shooter, provide the manifesto’s details, or explain the connection to Trump; the existing category also describes no documented claim in this account.
proposed_correction: Add reliable reporting on the shooter and manifesto, and specify the Trump statement or policy that makes this relevant to the timeline; otherwise remove the Trump framing and assign a suitable category.
